questions.question_text: Which core concept is central to the discussion in Section 1 of Understanding Scarcity and Trade-offs?
Which curve illustrates the maximum trade-off combinations of two goods an economy can produce?
According to Chapter 8, which factor plays a vital role in shaping societal or natural structures?
options: A) Scientific evidence and systematic processes
questions.correct_answer: A) Scientific evidence and systematic processes

questions.question_text: Define Opportunity Cost with a suitable economic example.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative foregone when a choice is made. Example: If a firm uses a piece of land to build a factory rather than renting it out for Rs. 50,000/month, the foregone Rs. 50,000 rent is the opportunity cost. Key points: Definition mentioning 'next best alternative foregone', Clear numerical or practical economic example

questions.question_text: What are the three central problems of an economy? Explain briefly.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) What to produce? Deciding which goods/services and quantities to produce given limited resources. 2) How to produce? Choosing production technique (Labor-intensive vs Capital-intensive). 3) For whom to produce? Determining distribution of national income and output among citizens.

questions.question_text: Explain why the Production Possibility Curve is concave to the origin.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) PPC is concave to the origin because of increasing Marginal Opportunity Cost (MOC). 2) Resources are specialized and not equally efficient in producing all goods. 3) When shifting resources from Good Y (Butter) to Good X (Guns), progressively less efficient resources are transferred. 4) Consequently, to produce each additional unit of Good X, an increasing quantity of Good Y must be sacrificed. 5) Increasing MOC causes the slope (Delta Y / Delta X) to steepen, producing a concave curve.

questions.question_text: Source Passage (Opportunity cost is the value of the foregone next best alte...): What does a point located inside the PPC signify?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: It signifies economic inefficiency, underutilization, or unemployment of available productive resources.

questions.question_text:
Read the scenario and answer the question:
'A developing country discovers major new technological automation techniques in agriculture, doubling crop output per hectare without needing additional land.'

Question: Explain how this technological breakthrough affects the country's PPC.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: The PPC shifts outwards (northeastern expansion), representing economic growth and an expanded production capability frontier due to technological progress.

image_asset.description: Economic graph displaying efficient, inefficient, and unattainable production points along the concave frontier

hotspots.label: Efficient Frontier Points
hotspots.description: Points ON the concave PPC represent maximum production with full resource utilization

hotspots.label: Inefficient Point
hotspots.description: Points INSIDE the curve reflect underemployed or inefficiently used resources

hotspots.label: Unattainable Point
hotspots.description: Points OUTSIDE the frontier cannot be produced with existing resources
